public_title: Why Extra Cash Burns out Brains 💸
hook: You work hard every week to earn more cash.

sections.title: Story
sections.narration: You work hard every week to earn more cash. That extra pay might actually stop raising your daily happiness after a set point. In 2010, researchers Daniel Kahneman and Angus Deaton at Princeton University analyzed about 450,000 survey responses. The result? Emotional well-being stopped rising after an annual income of about 75,000 dollars. Beyond that number, extra money bought life satisfaction, but not more daily joy. Is this just a modern American habit? A 2018 study led by Andrew Jebb at Purdue University looked at about 1.7 million people worldwide. They found a similar ceiling for daily happiness across every continent. So why do we assume more wealth always brings more joy? Evolutionary biologists explain that our brains evolved to seek short-term security, not endless accumulation. That constant drive kept hunter-gatherers alive, but it tricks modern workers into endless stress. So next time you chase a bigger paycheck, remember why you work hard every week to earn more cash.

claims.claim: Emotional well-being plateaus after earning about 75,000 dollars annually.
Satiation points for daily emotional happiness exist globally around similar income levels.
